name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and characterization of coordinated link-sharing, inauthentic networks and manipulation campaigns on Facebook and other platforms, from the original CooRnet/CLSB methodology to the VERA-AI Alert monitoring system. This is the researcher's longest-running and most active methodological line, spanning elections, health content and deceptive information operations across many countries.

name: Information Disorder & Disinformation Narratives
description: Monitoring and theorizing how false and misleading narratives (on topics such as the war in Ukraine, elections, and health) propagate within the hybrid media system, including the PROMPT project's narrative-tracking work and foundational taxonomy/definitional work on 'fake news' and misinformation.

name: Generative AI & Synthetic Media
description: Study of how generative AI is reshaping both the production of deceptive content (e.g. AI-generated imagery in coordinated gambling promotion) and the media landscape more broadly; reflected also in the new 'IA Generativa e Media' course and chapters on countering disinformation in the generative-AI era.

name: LLM-Assisted Research Methods
description: Development and validation of workflows that integrate large language models into computational content analysis and annotation pipelines (e.g. LLMs-in-the-loop, judge-agent systems, embedding-based clustering), addressing reliability, validity and disagreement in applying LLMs to social-scientific coding tasks.

name: Platform Governance & Research Data Access
description: Research and policy engagement on the conditions, tools and APIs available to study social media platforms, including the effects of the Digital Services Act, Meta's political content reduction policy, the CrowdTangle shutdown, and the methodological consequences of data-access thresholds; tied to the researcher's role as a DSA/ECAT independent expert.

name: Italian Electoral Communication
description: The MINE programme's core empirical focus: mapping Italian news media and political actors' social media activity across national election cycles (2018, 2019, 2022), including partisan attention scores, political parallelism, and party/institutional campaigns on Facebook and Instagram.

name: Political Polarization & Partisanship
description: Analysis of partisan community dynamics, affective engagement, insularity and cross-partisan interaction patterns around news, extending into comparative work on polarized public debate in Latin America and conceptual revisiting of 'polarization' as a key term in digital media research.

name: Health Misinformation & Fact-Checking
description: Mapping the circulation of problematic health information (COVID-19, vaccines, alternative medicine) on social media in Italy, India and Nigeria, and building tools and workflows to speed up fact-checking of nefarious health-related actors.

name: Social Media Affordances & Engagement
description: Studies of how platform design, algorithmic curation and affordances (reactions, shares, ad-recruitment tools) shape user engagement and visibility of political and media content, including systematic reviews of Facebook reactions and analyses of what drives large-scale visibility on the platform.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.

name: Survey Measurement Validity and Comparability
description: Papers examining methodological challenges in survey-based measurement, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how online sample composition and quality checks affect representativeness and response validity, and how question wording and dataset differences affect cross-national and longitudinal comparability of trust measures.
